key_insight: Combining physics-based simulation with neural networks identified an optimal tested HDPE friction stir welding condition of 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports weld-process selection to reduce void defects, moderate thermal gradients and stabilize axial forces in HDPE joints.
method: Model welding temperature, force, material flow and defects using a 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian simulation.
Train two multilayer perceptron neural networks on experimental temperature and axial-force histories.
Combine simulation and ANN predictions to map defective and defect-free processing windows.
evidence_signal: Experimentally validated simulations captured weld morphology and responses; ANNs achieved R² of 0.91–0.99, while 60 °C preheating reduced peak plunge force from 1600 N to approximately 1100 N.
watch_item: Predictive accuracy and the reported optimum are established within the tested parameter space; other geometries, HDPE grades or operating conditions require validation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
